pr_title: Server-side syntax highlighting for all code
pr_body: This PR does a few things: * Remove all traces of highlight.js * Use [chroma ](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma) library to provide fast syntax highlighting directly on the server * Provide syntax highlighting for diffs + code comments * Re-style code view and unified/split diffs views to try and look a bit more 'modern' * Add custom syntax highlighting styling for regular theme and convert previous arc-green highlighting best I could Fixes #7729 Fixes #10157 Fixes #11825 Fixes #7728 Fixes #3872 Fixes #3682 And perhaps gets closer to #9553 Suggestions welcome for styling New Diff:
pr_comments: I think you still need to run `npm uninstall highlight.js` and commit the results.

> I think you still need to run `npm uninstall highlight.js` and commit the results.

Thanks! fixed
Oh, and `npm uninstall domino` as well and remove [this line](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/4b66d9ad980aa9d84f4496cee67bcef0b82d643c/webpack.config.js#L63).

> Oh, and `npm uninstall domino` as well and remove [this line](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/4b66d9ad980aa9d84f4496cee67bcef0b82d643c/webpack.config.js#L63).

fixed
Those suggestions above should fix some of colors that are definitely too dark in `arc-green` for sufficient contrast. Are there any themes for Chroma we could maybe use as a baseline?

This looks to work quite nicely from a bit of testing.

I wonder if we need a mechanism to stop highlighting big files if they take too long, either based on processing time or line count. I think GitHub just stops highlighting around line 20k in a single file.

@silverwind I tried a few but they looked weird on dark green as-is so I tried to just copy the values that were present before. I  don't use/enjoy dark themes so I'm certainly not the best judge probably (I think he current one is difficult to look at too).

If you want to try and test how some look on dark green, I think the quickest way would be to set this to false so it uses inline styles for the moment:

 https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/1bb78a013d55767d80d732bbd9ea752b8f1d2416/modules/highlight/highlight.go#L85

and then you can try different themes here (where it says styles.GitHub now).

 https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/1bb78a013d55767d80d732bbd9ea752b8f1d2416/modules/highlight/highlight.go#L116

Heres a list

 https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/tree/master/styles

I'll commit the changes above as well

Will check the themes later. I'm thinking we could probably use these colors, at least as the baseline:

Light: https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/blob/master/styles/github.go
Dark: https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/blob/master/styles/solarized-dark.go

I used the Github one as a baseline for light but I think it is either too old or was just bad because it looks nothing like Github does (as you can tell I still tried my best to just copy what Github does in all of the light sections).

I'll add file size limit to rendering later too -- I thought we already had a limit for this but it is just the general UI display limit which is 8MB so that isn't helpful here.

GitHub at one time used pygments so I assume that theme is based on it. They're now using the Prettylights highlighter (closed source), but I found this which may be of use:

https://github.com/primer/github-syntax-theme-generator

Noticed we don't need the `worker-loader` either now, so you can `npm uninstall worker-loader`, then remove these lines:

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/b918609acc11d2deb1dd2182597c7cbb3624dbdb/webpack.config.js#L116-L129

And finally remove the first entry here:

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/master/.eslintrc#L31
@silverwind limited size to 25kb and made those js changes thanks

@silverwind made a few tweaks to light theme based on the link you gave above -- think it is pretty good for now. Pygments doesn't have quite the level of detail that pretty lights does in some areas but is pretty close.

Also raised the threshold for highlighting to 1MB based on https://help.github.com/en/github/creating-cloning-and-archiving-repositories/limits-for-viewing-content-and-diffs-in-a-repository

Will likely need to undo to `worker-loader` removal (part of https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/12047/commits/901ce59785e65bd21c83d189cb3d111d7e3254d2) because https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/12095 will depend on it.

> Will likely need to undo to `worker-loader` removal (part of [901ce59](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/commit/901ce59785e65bd21c83d189cb3d111d7e3254d2)) because #12095 will depend on it.

Do I need to do any special commands to properly add it back to npm, or just add the line back to package.json and run make frontend?
Run `npm install worker-loader` and add back the two removed sections in `webpack.config.js` and `.eslintrc`. `npm install` will take care of `package-lock.json`.
Syntax looks good on light and dark. I have not encountered some of the more exotic identifiers in the files I was looking at but we should be good with those brighter color on arc-green.

issue_context.title: Code blocks in Wiki are rendered with arbitrary syntax highlighting instead of none
issue_context.body:
- Gitea version (or commit ref): 1.11.5 - Can you reproduce the bug at https://try.gitea.io: - [X] Yes: https://try.gitea.io/qwertfisch/markdown-test/wiki/Code-blocks - [ ] No - [ ] Not relevant ## Description When adding a code block on a page in the built-in wiki, but with no language given for syntax highlighting, this block will be rendered using an arbitrarily chosen highlighting. Code blocks without selected syntax I will set like this: ~~~ ``` This is simple text rendered with fixed-width font, but no syntax highlighting. ``` ~~~ Even if the text inside the block would contain keywords for *some* languages, I do not expect them to be highlighted or rendered other than as fixed-width font. In fact when given no language for the code block, I expect the language to be *None*. ### Actual result When selecting the preview window, or after storing the page, a second later a seemingly arbitrarily chosen syntax highlighting is applied to the block. On the [example page](https://try.gitea.io/qwertfisch/markdown-test/wiki/Code-blocks) I added some keywords (for some languages), and the two blocks are rendered as Cal and Vim, respectively. It seems the highlighting is selected automatically given the content of the block. ### Workaround I can enclose the block with `
` / `
` instead of Markdown. Is there otherwise a possibility to have a non-syntaxed code block with Markdown syntax? **Edit:** `
` does not set the content to a fixed-width font, so this is unfortunately no solution.

Is this a bug for Gitea? Or should I file a bug on the Markdown interpreter used (goldmark?).
comments:
This is not the fault of goldmark.

Gitea uses highlightjs for syntax highlighting of code blocks and as far as I understand highlightjs will automatically attempt to detect the language.

It's probable that if you put `plaintext` after the backticks that would turn it off.
Valid bug. We should put the `plaintext` class on `<code>` to prevent hljs from autodetection in case the user did not specify a language in markdown.

An automatically selected highlighting is welcome – just not when it is not expected. I could not find a documentation of this feature before. 

`plaintext` works and selects the plaintext syntax from hljs, thanks for the advice. Also any other name unknown for hljs would work and use a `language-[name]` class, which defaults to no highlighting.
